SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of School Suggested vocabulary: school, classroom, desk, chair, table, field, gate, in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Which words do we use to talk about school? 2. How can we listen attentively to others?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self –Efficacy: learner’s knowledge of their school is enhanced as they sing songs and recite poems about their school.

• Digital literacy: learner’s ability to create with technology is enhanced as they use tablets, mobile phones, laptops to take pictures of

things around the school.

Values:
• Respect: enhanced as the learner understands and appreciate others when they are playing language games.

• Responsibility: enhanced as the learner observes safety precautions during nature walk.

Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Life skills: Self-awareness is nurtured as they independently take photos and identify the general features of their school during a nature walk

11

Link to other Learning Areas:

Environmental Activities: as learners relate to things found in the environment during a nature walk while taking pictures of things found in

school.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices with filter

keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand, adapted cameras such as those with grips.

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
